samples.summary: Nested docs-table walk inside a slide text body skips null rows/cells, storing a shape the docs table layout crashes on
samples.evidence: In `assertValidSlideBlocks` the nested `tableData` walk does `const cells = (rows[r] as { cells?: unknown })?.cells; if (!Array.isArray(cells)) continue;` (line 922) and `if (cell === undefined || cell === null) continue;` (line 927). A `null` row or `null` cell is therefore accepted verbatim and persisted by `writeSlidesRoot`. The docs table layout that renders those blocks dereferences both unconditionally: `const cell = row.cells[c]` (packages/docs/src/view/table-layout.ts:157) throws on a null row, and `for (const block of cell.blocks)` (table-layout.ts:291) is only guarded by `!cell`. This is exactly the failure mode the sibling `assertValidTableData` was changed to repair for slide tables (`rows[r] = { height: 0, cells: [] }`, `cells[c] = { body: { blocks: [] }, style: {} }`, lines 779/801) and that the docs arm rejects (`if (!cell || !Array.isArray(cell.blocks)) throw`, line 400). Only this third copy of the walk lets it through, so a deck can still be stored in a shape that is a TypeError for every viewer.

samples.summary: New MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH cap covers only the element walk; the tableData/text-body recursion on the same endpoint is still unbounded
samples.evidence: `MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH = 32` is checked in `assertValidElementData` (line 651) and its own comment gives the reason: "the walk recurses through `data.children` and the JSON body limit is 25 MB — enough for a compact payload to exhaust the stack on an authenticated endpoint." The two other recursions reachable from the same handler have no ceiling at all: `assertValidBlock` → cell.blocks → `assertValidBlock` (lines 405-410) in the docs arm, and `assertValidSlideBlocks` → `assertValidTextBodyBlocks` → `assertValidSlideBlocks` (lines 937/880) for docs tables nested inside slide text bodies. A body of the form {"slides":[…{"data":{"blocks":[{"tableData":{"rows":[{"cells":[{"blocks":[…nested…]}]}]}}]}}]} nests ~50 bytes per level, so the 25 MB limit allows tens of thousands of levels — a RangeError thrown mid-walk, after the repairs have already mutated part of the body, surfacing as a 500 rather than the intended 400.

samples.summary: `typeof x !== 'object'` checks let an array through for inline.style and docs cell.style, while the sibling block-style check rejects arrays
samples.evidence: `normalizeSlideInlines` uses `if (typeof inline.style !== 'object')` (line 1000) and the docs arm uses `if (!inline.style || typeof inline.style !== 'object')` (line 442) and `if (!cell.style || typeof cell.style !== 'object')` (line 415). `typeof [] === 'object'`, so an array is accepted and stored verbatim. The block-style check added in the same change deliberately adds the array test (`typeof block.style !== 'object' || Array.isArray(block.style)`, line 906) and the diff's own commentary explains why an array must not be accepted where a record is expected. The three checks above are the same sink and were left inconsistent.

samples.summary: `toXmlInt` coerces null/''/[] to 0 instead of using the caller's fallback
samples.evidence: `function toXmlInt(value, fallback) { const n = Number(value); return String(Number.isFinite(n) ? Math.round(n) : fallback); }` — `Number(null)`, `Number('')` and `Number([])` are all 0, which is finite, so a persisted `durationMs: null` emits `dur="0"` instead of the intended 500 and `pptxPreset.id: null` emits `presetID="0"` (not a valid OOXML preset id) instead of the fallback 1. The whole point of the helper is to substitute the fallback for values that are not real numbers; only NaN/Infinity currently reach that branch.

samples.summary: Partial block-style serializer + merge-only styleByPath can leave a stale CRDT attribute while the local cache advances
samples.evidence: `applyBlockStyle` computes `merged = normalizeBlockStyle({ ...block.style, ...style })` and writes `attrs = serializeBlockStyle(merged)` via `tree.styleByPath` (merge-only), then unconditionally updates the cache (`block.style = merged`). `normalizeBlockStyle` is `{ ...DEFAULT_BLOCK_STYLE, ...style }` (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:273), so an explicitly-undefined or non-finite field survives into `merged`; the new `serializeBlockStyleAttrs` then *omits* that attribute (crdt-attrs.ts:69-71) instead of overwriting it as the old serializer did. The CRDT therefore keeps the previous value while the local cached document holds the new (undefined/NaN) one — a silent divergence from remote peers until reload. The same applies to `setBlockType`'s `Object.assign(attrs, serializeBlockStyle(materializedStyle))` (line 1438).

samples.summary: Repairing an absent columnWidths to [] on a table that has rows silently renders the table with no columns
samples.evidence: `assertValidTableData` does `if (widths === undefined || widths === null) { data.columnWidths = []; }` (line 758) and then continues to walk non-empty `rows`. `drawTable` sizes columns from `data.columnWidths`, so the repaired deck is persisted with populated rows and zero columns — the cells become unrenderable rather than the caller getting a 400 telling them the width list is missing. Repairing to `[]` is only semantically neutral when `rows` is also empty.

samples.summary: PRST_BY_KIND's `satisfies` does not enforce exhaustiveness, so a future ShapeKind silently exports as rect
samples.evidence: `(... ] as const satisfies readonly Exclude<ShapeKind, 'freeform'>[]).map(...)` only proves every listed entry *is* a ShapeKind; it does not prove every ShapeKind is listed. `kindToPrst` returns `PRST_BY_KIND.get(kind) ?? 'rect'`, so any kind omitted from the literal degrades to a rectangle with no compile error and no test failure. I diffed the literal against the `ShapeKind` union in packages/slides/src/model/element.ts:54-125 and it is currently complete, so this is a trap rather than a live bug; a `Record<Exclude<ShapeKind,'freeform'>, string>` seed (or a mapped-type check) would make omissions a tsc error.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repo: the nested tableData walk in assertValidSlideBlocks skips null/malformed rows (`(rows[r] as { cells?: unknown })?.cells; if (!Array.isArray(cells)) continue;`, docs-content.controller.ts:922-923) and null cells (line 927), leaving them in the object that is persisted by writeSlidesRoot (validation at line 158 precedes the write at line 198, and the file states slide text bodies are stored verbatim with no read codec). The sibling slide-table validator repairs the same shapes (lines 779, 801) and the docs arm rejects them (lines 393, 400), so this third copy is the only leak. The consumer crashes on it: packages/docs/src/view/table-layout.ts:154-157 does `const row = rows[r]; ... row.cells[c]` with no null check (also 193, 206, 247, 289), and that function is reached for slide text bodies via packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts:400-403 (`block.type === 'table' && block.tableData` -> computeTableLayout), which slides invokes through `computeLayout` imported from @wafflebase/docs in packages/slides/src/view/canvas/text-renderer.ts:3. No guard elsewhere repairs a null row on read, so the stored deck is a TypeError for viewers. Real, in-lane (missing guard / stored crashing state), and blocking.

The two sibling recursions on the same PUT handler take no depth argument: assertValidBlock recurses into table cell blocks (405-410, signature at 365) and assertValidSlideBlocks -> assertValidTextBodyBlocks (937) -> assertValidSlideBlocks (880) form an unbounded cycle (signatures 866-869, 888). Result is a RangeError escaping as a 500 instead of the intended 400, after in-place repairs have already mutated part of the caller's body. No named refutation ground applies.

finding.summary: Reviewer did not produce a valid verdict: review: every credential in the pool (2) was retired — nothing left to fail over to

verdict.reason: The finding names no file, line, or condition and describes no code behavior. Its text is the runtime output of the other reviewer's own agent harness exhausting its API credential pool ("Reviewer did not produce a valid verdict"). The message originates from an intentional, documented fail-fast guard in scripts/agent/ask.mjs:594-601, which throws when tokenPool().isExhausted() with kind="pool-exhausted" and retryable=false, precisely so the caller's withRetry does not back off on a condition that cannot clear in-run (rationale comment at ask.mjs:587-593; failover loop at ask.mjs:611-619). The quoted wording ("was retired") does not even match the repository string ("has hit its usage limit"), confirming it is a paraphrased runtime notice rather than cited code. No logic error, missing guard, crash path, async mistake, swallowed error, or broken invariant is asserted or present, so there is no defect "as described" for the Correctness lens to evaluate — this is a reviewer-infrastructure re-run concern, not a repository defect.
